questions.question: Name the crops the early farmers grew and describe the farming year.
questions.expected_answer: They grew sorghum, millet, cowpeas, jugo beans, melons and gourds. Fields were cleared in winter and spring, planted with iron hoes when the summer rains came, weeded in summer while children scared birds away, and harvested in late summer and autumn. Tired fields were left to rest.

questions.question: Explain how grain was stored and turned into food.
questions.expected_answer: Grain was dried, threshed and winnowed, then stored in pits, often in the cattle kraal, or in raised granaries to keep out rats, damp and insects. Women ground it on a grindstone into flour, which was cooked as porridge. Sorghum was also brewed into beer.

questions.question: Explain why cattle were so useful to the early farmers.
questions.expected_answer: Cattle gave milk, eaten as sour milk, and meat at special occasions. Their hides made clothing, bags and shields, their horns made containers, and their dung was used for floors, plaster and fuel. They were also a family's wealth.
